description_en: Rādhākṛṣṇa Mandira, located on Svatha square, collapsed during the earthquake 2015, and was rebuilt in 2022. The three- tiered temple stands on three plinths. 13 steps lead to the wood-carved main doorway flanked by two lions in a sitting position facing east. Next to the lions, there used to be two statues of guardian deities which were stolen in the 1990s. According to local informants, the original main deities in the sanctum were also stolen prior to 1967. During the 1967 renovations, new stone statues of Rādhā Kriṣṇa, Viṣṇu and Lakṣmī were installed and consecrated. However, a few years later these newly placed images were stolen yet again. The dailynityapūjāused to be performed by a Rājopādhyāya priest, but currently no particular seasonal or annual rituals are performed at the temple."Raised on a triple-stepped plinth and an additional platform, the pyramidal temple of three successive roofs dominates the square and is visible from the Darbar Square. The temple underwent several restoration schemes in the 19th century, in 1967, 1982 and in 1993-94. After the middle roof collapsed on 30th May 1989, the Kathmandu Valley Preservation Trust restored the temple in collaboration with the Department of Archaeology between 1992-93. During this restoration all roofs were renewed, five missing blind windows on the ground floor were replaced, reinforced concrete ring beams were introduced on top of the masonry core and on top of the wall carried by the pillars of the circuambulatory. Only seven of the 52 struts date to the 17th century.” (Gutschow 2011, 478) After its collapse in the 2015 earthquakes, reconstruction work started in ca. 2017 but was abandoned in early 2018 due to the poor quality of the restoration work. In2020,a new contractor was engaged and restoration work concluded in 2022.“The Radha Krishna carvings are comparable stylistically with those at Svatha Narayan [Temple], although it may be mentioned that the larger size and artistic expressiveness of the Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa elements make them far more expressive” (KVPT1992, 6). The ground floor door frames feature carvings of Bhairava, Sālabhañjikā, Aṣṭamātṛkā, Garuḍa and different incarnations of Viṣṇu.The principal figures on the lower struts are male-female (Śiva-Śakti) images, and there are two single Bhairava figures. The principal figures on the struts for the middle of the roof are male gods, most of which are different forms of Viṣṇu. Aṣṭamātṛkās are depicted on the upper roof struts.No inscriptions exist that provide the construction date of the temple. According to theBhāṣā Vaṁsāvali(p. 69), the temple's construction is attributed to Kriti Singh Malla, the illegitimate son of King Siddhi Narasiṃha Malla, who built it in 1668. The Raghuvaṃśī family living in the vicinity of the temple claim to be the descendants of Kriti Singh Malla.
description_ne: राधाकृष्णमन्दिर स्वथमा अवस्थित रहेको छ । यस मन्दिरको निर्माण सम्बन्धि जानकारी दिने कुनै पनि अभिलेख अहिलेसम्म प्राप्त भएको छैन ।भाषावंशावलीमा (पृ. ६९) यो मन्दिर राजा कीर्त्ति सिंह मल्ल (राजा सिद्धि नरसिंह मल्लका अवैधानिक श्रीमति पट्टिका छोरा) ले सन् १६६८ मा बनाएको उल्लेख छ । मन्दिर परिसर नजिकै बसोवास गर्ने रघुवंशी परिवारका सदस्यहरू अहिले पनि आफुहरू कीर्त्ति सिंह मल्लका दरसन्तान भएको विश्वास गर्दछन् । यो मन्दिरको दोश्रो तल्लाको छानो सन् १९८९ मे महिनाको ३० तारिकमा भत्केपछाडि काठमाडौं उपत्यका संरक्षण कोष र राष्ट्रिय पुरातत्त्व विभागद्वारा सन् १९९२-९३ मा संयुक्त रूपमा यो मन्दिरको जीर्णोद्धार गरिएको थियो ।

historical_events.event_description: Construction of the original temple according toBhāṣā Vaṁśāvalī.
Restoration of the temple. New stone statues were installed in the temple's sanctuary as the originals had been stolen.

Restoration of the temple. The work consisted ofsurkhipointing on the ground floor façade and uppermost plinth. New stone paving replaced the historical stone and tiles of the ambulatory and sanctuary.
Restoration of the temple by the Kathmandu Valley Preservation Trust and the Department of Archaeology.
During the 2015 earthquake, the temple collapsed completely. Some salvaged materials such as temple struts were moved to the archaeological garden in Patan where they were stored in the open.
Rādhākṛṣṇa Mandira was finally reconstructed in early 2022, after many failed attempts to do so.
